clue.text: Just girl entering area: in it bombs

indicators.note: something that bombs is blown apart, so the letters before it are scattered into a new order
the girl goes into the middle of the other letters, as someone entering a room is inside it

blocks.note: gal is informal for a girl
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl wanders into a war zone where bombs are falling.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters give EITARIAN, and GAL slips in after the first letter to make EGALITARIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An egalitarian society is a fair one, treating everyone as equal, which is what just means here.

clue.text: Idler, lovely and free

blocks.note: something lovely is good
free of charge, costing nothing

explanation.surface: A lazy person is described as charming and footloose.
explanation.walkthrough: GOOD plus FOR NOTHING gives GOOD-FOR-NOTHING.
explanation.definitionFit: A good-for-nothing is a worthless, lazy person, a synonym for an idler or wastrel.

clue.text: Instrument fibber heard

indicators.note: heard tells us to go by how the word for a fibber is spoken, not how it is spelt

blocks.note: a fibber is a liar, which is pronounced the same as the harp-like instrument

explanation.surface: Someone hears an instrument played by a known teller of tales.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyre is a small stringed instrument of ancient Greece, an example of a musical instrument.

clue.text: Metallic element: I hide one in stomach

indicators.note: in places the first group of letters inside the word for the stomach

blocks.note: taken as written
to tan is to beat, to hide someone; also hide is tanned
the Roman numeral for one
tum is informal for the stomach

explanation.surface: A confession: I am hiding something inside my belly, which is made of metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb about concealment, but to tan someone's hide is to thrash them, so hide and tan are both verbs for beating.
explanation.definitionFit: Titanium is a strong, light chemical element classed among the metals, element number 22.

clue.text: List one short — as may be cosmetic?

indicators.note: short means the word for one is cut and loses its final letter

blocks.note: a roll is a list of names
taken as written

explanation.surface: A register is one name short, perhaps only for show.
explanation.walkthrough: ROLL plus ONE minus its last letter gives ROLL-ON. The question mark flags that the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A roll-on is an applicator with a rolling ball, used for deodorants and other toiletries and cosmetics.

clue.text: Where spinner achieves turn, a big hit coming up

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the big hit is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
in cricket a six is the biggest hit, clearing the boundary

explanation.surface: A cricket spin bowler gets the ball to turn, and a six comes along.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket setting suggests a spin bowler, but the spinner is anything that rotates. A six is cricket's maximum hit.
explanation.definitionFit: An axis is the line about which a spinning object rotates, so it is where any spinner turns.

clue.text: Novel is a right cheat, with a leading author

indicators.note: novel means new, so the following letters are made into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written, joining the rest of the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A book review claims a crime novel is a swindle, alongside a bestselling writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a noun fitting the author theme, but it is the anagram signal; 'with' joins the two parts of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha Christie, creator of Poirot and Miss Marple, is the best-selling novelist of all time.

clue.text: Decalitre emptied over dry allotment, damage done

indicators.note: emptied means the word has its insides removed, leaving only its first and last letters
in a down clue, over means the first piece is placed above the pieces that follow

blocks.note: the outside letters of the unit
sec is the wine term for dry
a ration is an allotted share

explanation.surface: A measure of water poured on a dry garden allotment has caused harm.
explanation.walkthrough: The garden allotment picture hides a share or quota. SEC is the French word used on wine labels for dry.
explanation.definitionFit: Desecration is violation or spoiling of something sacred, so damage done to it.

clue.text: I'm evidently being informed, I know!

blocks.note: first meaning, read literally: someone is telling me something
second meaning: the idiom of emphatic agreement

explanation.walkthrough: The same phrase works literally, describing being told something, and as the idiom meaning that you agree completely.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is a colloquial way to agree strongly, meaning I am well aware of that already.

clue.text: All in ad dancing around in stockings — sauce!

indicators.note: dancing letters move around and end up in a new order
around tells us the word for stockings wraps the rearranged letters

blocks.note: hose is an old word for stockings or tights
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An advert shows everyone dancing in their stockings, which is rather saucy.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation 'sauce!' sounds like a cry of cheek at the risqué advert, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hollandaise is a rich sauce of butter, egg yolk and lemon, served with fish or eggs Benedict.

clue.text: Hooked by warrior, fearsome fish

indicators.note: hooked by means caught inside the following words, so the letters lie within them

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A fierce fish is caught on a line by a fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: The orfe, or ide, is a freshwater fish of the carp family, often kept in ornamental ponds.

clue.text: Bulb working with this person about

blocks.note: a machine that is working is on
the setter speaking of themself
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: Someone fiddles with a light bulb, working around it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This person' is the setter referring to themself, so it means I.
explanation.definitionFit: An onion is a vegetable that grows as a bulb, the swollen underground part of the plant.

clue.text: Pen name, ultimately, that may prove an irritation

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word before it

blocks.note: a pen for pigs is a sty
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A writer's pseudonym, in the end, turns out to be annoying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen name' reads as a pseudonym, but pen is an animal enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, an irritation of the eye.

clue.text: Hand round second song

indicators.note: round means the word for a hand goes about the other letter

blocks.note: the palm is the inside of the hand
s is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: Someone passes round a second song, as at a sing-song.
explanation.definitionFit: A psalm is a sacred song or hymn, especially one from the biblical Book of Psalms.

clue.text: Originally lost, item of jewellery in corner

indicators.note: originally lost means the very first letter has gone missing

blocks.note: a bangle is a rigid bracelet

explanation.surface: A lost piece of jewellery is first found in a corner.
explanation.definitionFit: An angle is the space where two lines or walls meet, so a corner.

clue.text: Plant egg behind bird

indicators.note: behind means the first piece comes after the next one in the answer

blocks.note: the lark is a songbird
to egg on is to spur on

explanation.surface: Someone places an egg behind a bird, as if planting it in a nest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egg' looks like a noun but is the verb, as in egging someone on.
explanation.definitionFit: Larkspur is a garden flower related to delphiniums, with spikes of blue or purple blooms.

clue.text: Cruel fashion in a fur

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape or make, so the letters are reshaped into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Fashion in fur is cruel to animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Cruel treatment is harsh and unjust, which is unfair, a loose synonym.

clue.text: Heading for Hawick, a poet in Scottish town

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: the first letter of the place name
taken as written
John Milton, poet of Paradise Lost

explanation.surface: A poet heads for Hawick, a Borders town in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Hawick is itself a Scottish town, which makes it look like the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamilton is a large town in South Lanarkshire, south-east of Glasgow.

clue.text: Having shaken off lead, dog goes after last of Italian pasta

indicators.note: a dog that has shaken off its lead loses its leading letter here
last of points to the final letter of the next word
goes after means the first piece follows the second in the answer

blocks.note: the final letter of the word
a breed of dog

explanation.surface: A dog slips its leash and chases after the Italian's pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: The lead is the dog's leash in the picture, but here it means its first letter. N plus POODLE minus P gives NOODLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A noodle is a strip of pasta, made from flour and egg dough.

clue.text: Flier maybe almost hit, nearly destroyed

indicators.note: nearly means the word before it is not quite complete, losing its last letter
something destroyed is smashed up, so its letters are rebuilt in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, though it looks like an instruction
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pilot was almost struck and his plane nearly destroyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' reads as a deletion signal, but it is plain fodder; 'nearly' is the one that trims the word hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A mailshot is a batch of advertising sent by post, and a printed flier is one example.

clue.text: Engrossed, camping?

blocks.note: first meaning: wholly absorbed in something
second meaning, split into two words: inside canvas shelter

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark warns that the second meaning splits the word in two, describing someone sleeping under canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: Intent as an adjective means concentrating hard, absorbed, as in intent on her book.

clue.text: A retiring grey

blocks.note: taken as written
a retiring person is shy

explanation.surface: A quiet, unassuming person is a grey sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashy means pale grey, like the colour of ash, a synonym.

clue.text: Slowcoach taking cruise round pole

indicators.note: round means the word for cruise wraps about the other letter

blocks.note: to cruise is to sail
N for north, a magnetic pole

explanation.surface: A dawdler takes a cruise around the North Pole.
explanation.walkthrough: The pole is N, for north, one of the magnetic poles.
explanation.definitionFit: A snail is a byword for slowness, so a slowcoach can be called one figuratively.

clue.text: Top off initially in pool

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it

blocks.note: a lid is a top
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Swimmers take their tops off at the swimming pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top off' reads as undressing, but they are separate pieces. A lido is a British term for a public outdoor swimming pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A lido is a public open-air swimming pool, especially in Britain.

clue.text: Lengthy vehicle in showroom I looked up

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the words that follow
in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, the pronoun and the start of the last word

explanation.surface: Someone browsed a long car in a dealer's showroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A limo, short for limousine, is a luxurious car, often a stretched and very long one.

clue.text: Map book missing capital of Tunisia, sadly

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its first, capital letter
missing means the book has lost that letter

blocks.note: an atlas is a book of maps
the first letter of the country

explanation.surface: A map book sadly lacks the capital of Tunisia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital of Tunisia' wants to be Tunis; it is only the letter T. ATLAS without T gives ALAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Alas is an exclamation of grief or regret, so it can replace sadly as a comment adverb.

clue.text: Schmaltz delivered in Italy met with irritation

indicators.note: irritation stirs things up, so the letters are agitated into a new order

blocks.note: something delivered has been sent
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Mawkish feeling met with annoyance on its arrival in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Schmaltz is excessive sentimentality, especially in music or film; the word comes from Yiddish for chicken fat.

clue.text: Clearing table perhaps, left building in garden

blocks.note: in snooker or pool, potting every ball clears the table
shed is a past form meaning cast off, left behind

explanation.surface: Someone clearing a table perhaps left a building in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: Clearing a table suggests tidying dishes, but it is snooker, where you pot balls until none are left.
explanation.definitionFit: A potting shed is a garden hut where plants are potted up and tools kept.
